newsitem.title: USA: Plaintiffs near resting in Fla. tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Plaintiffs near resting in Fla. tobacco case.

text.p: Attorneys for the plaintiffs in a wrongful death suit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co said they were close to resting their case on Wednesday.

Attorneys for Reynolds were expected to present their case starting Wednesday afternoon. David Townsend, a Reynolds' research and development employee who specializes in cigarette design, was expected to be the first defense witness.
Late Wednesday morning, attorneys for the plaintiffs sought Judge Bernard Nachman's permission to show the jury a videotape of Jean Connor made less than two months before she died.
Plaintiff Dana Raulerson sued Reynolds on behalf of the estate and children of Connor, her sister, who died of lung cancer at age 49.
The tape shows Connor, weak, gaunt and bald after chemotherapy, speaking in a weakened voice and displaying scars on her arms she said resulted from taking cancer drugs.
Nachman told Raulerson's attorney, Norwood "Woody" Wilner, to stop the tape after about 90 seconds. "Stop the tape. Stop the tape," he ordered.

"To watch even that much of it is emotionally overwhelming to me," he said, noting that the suffering of the decedent is not an element of damages in a wrongful death suit. "...If I am so disturbed by what I just saw, I imagine a jury would be as well," he said, saying the tape should not be admitted into evidence.
Wilner said he would edit the five-minute tape, which originally had been 15 minutes long, down to one minute and show it to Nachman again after the lunch break.
Also on Wednesday, the plaintiffs dismissed their own civil conspiracy claim from the suit. Outside the courtroom, Wilner said the suit had gotten too unwieldy to pursue every claim.

But Paul Crist, lead counsel for Reynolds, said the court had already rejected most of the civil conspiracy claim. "The court had granted summary judgement with respect to 75 percent of it before trial, so there was nothing left," he said.
R.J. Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp
